- TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_of_trivial_complement (example): G′ trivial (G′ = 1, G_p = G, χ = 1): under the identification O[G] ≅ O[G_p] induced by G ≅ G_p, π_1 is that identification, and componentEquiv composed with the restriction R_Ĝ → R_{Ψ_1} (Ψ_1 is the set of all characters) and with TauCeti.charGroupRing.equivGroupRing is that identification.
- TauCeti.charGroupRing.componentEquiv_of_trivial_sylow (example): G_p trivial (G′ = G, G_p = 1): Ψ_χ = {χ}, π_χ(x) = ev_χ(x)·1 in O[G_p], which is O through its structure map, and componentEquiv(α_{Ψ_χ}(g′)) = χ(g′)·1.

- componentProj_sign (computation): G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd, χ the sign character: π_χ(h·g_p) = −g_p for g_p ∈ G_p, π_χ((1 − h)/2) = 1 and π_χ((1 + h)/2) = 0.

#### O[G] is the product of its components R_χ

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/group-ring-component-decomposition** — theorem.

Write G = G_p × G′. The idempotents e_χ ∈ O[G], χ ∈ Ĝ′, are pairwise orthogonal with sum 1, and the O-algebra homomorphism O[G] → ∏_{χ∈Ĝ′} R_{Ψ_χ}, x ↦ (α_{Ψ_χ}(x))_χ, is an isomorphism. The sets Ψ_χ, χ ∈ Ĝ′, partition Ĝ.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.bijective_proj_components`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- #G′ is a unit of O, and O contains the values of the characters of G′ because the exponent of G′ divides that of G.
- The idempotents e_ω and their relations are those of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition and its relation lemmas, which are stated for O a complete discrete valuation ring with finite residue field of characteristic p and a finite abelian group H with p ∤ #H; both hold here for H = G′.

Construction or proof route:

- In O[G′] the idempotents e_χ are orthogonal (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition-api-1) with sum 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/character-decomposition-api-2). The O-algebra homomorphism O[G′] → O[G] induced by the inclusion (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom) carries both relations to O[G], so (e_χ)_χ is a complete family of orthogonal idempotents of O[G].
- CompleteOrthogonalIdempotents.bijective_pi: O[G] → ∏_χ O[G]/(1 − e_χ) is bijective.
- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/component-character-group-ring, (1 − e_χ)O[G] = ker α_{Ψ_χ}, so O[G]/(1 − e_χ) ≅ R_{Ψ_χ} compatibly with the projections from O[G] (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.quotientKerEquiv); composing gives the stated isomorphism.
- Every ψ ∈ Ĝ restricts to exactly one χ ∈ Ĝ′, so the sets Ψ_χ are pairwise disjoint with union Ĝ. Each Ψ_χ is nonempty, because g′g_p ↦ χ(g′) is a character of G = G_p × G′ that restricts to χ. So the sets Ψ_χ partition Ĝ.

#### Norm quotients of a component

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/component-norm-quotient** — theorem.

(Dasgupta–Kakde Corollary 2.3.) For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and a subgroup I ⊆ G (the source takes I ⊆ G_p), R_χ/N_I R_χ ≅ R_Ψ with Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ, ψ(I) ≠ 1}; precisely, ker α_Ψ is generated by 1 − e_χ and N_I. In particular R_χ/N_I is a finite-index subring of a finite product of copies of O.

#### Units of character group rings

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-criterion** — theorem.

For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ and x ∈ R_Ψ: x is a unit of R_Ψ iff ψ(x) ∈ O^× for every ψ ∈ Ψ, and this holds iff ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} ψ(x) ∈ O^×. No locality of R_Ψ is assumed.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.isUnit_iff`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- Only that O is a commutative ring and that Ψ is finite is used.

Construction or proof route:

- The inclusion R_Ψ ⊆ ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O is an injective integral ring homomorphism: ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O is a finite O-module (Ψ is finite), so each of its elements is integral over O (IsIntegral.of_finite), hence over the O-subalgebra R_Ψ (IsIntegral.tower_top for the tower O → R_Ψ → ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O). An injective integral ring homomorphism is local (RingHom.IsIntegral.isLocalHom: the inverse y of x in the product satisfies a monic equation y^n + a_1y^{n−1} + … + a_n = 0 over R_Ψ, and multiplying by x^{n−1} gives y = −(a_1 + a_2x + … + a_nx^{n−1}) ∈ R_Ψ). So if every ψ(x) is a unit of O, then x is a unit of the product (Pi.isUnit_iff) and therefore of R_Ψ.
- Conversely the coordinate maps R_Ψ → O are ring homomorphisms, so they send units to units.
- A finite product of elements of the commutative ring O is a unit iff every factor is (IsUnit.prod_iff).

Immediate prerequisites:

Acceptance controls:

- G = C_p, x = g ∈ R_Ĝ = O[C_p]: every ψ(g) is a root of unity, so g is a unit (with inverse g^{p−1}).
- x = g − 1 in O[C_p]: ψ(x) = 0 for ψ = 1, so x is not a unit.
- R_Ψ need not be local: for p ∤ #G, G ≠ 1 and Ψ = Ĝ, R_Ĝ = ∏_{ψ} O is a product of #G ≥ 2 copies of O, and the criterion is the description of the units of a product.

Source locators:

- DK-arXiv-v3 — §2.3, arXiv v3 PDF p. 18. The source uses the criterion for the character group ring O[G]^− (all odd characters), which is not local as soon as G′ has more than one odd character, and gives no proof; the first step above proves it for every Ψ.
- DK-arXiv-v3 — §5.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34. For the local ring R = O[G_p]_χ the source passes from ∏ψ(x) ∈ O^× to every ψ(x) ∈ O^× and then to x ∈ R^×, giving as reason that the maps R → O are local homomorphisms of local rings.

#### Units of a character group ring of one component are detected by one character

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character** — lemma.

Let χ ∈ Ĝ′ and let Ψ be a nonempty subset of Ψ_χ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ}. For x ∈ R_Ψ the following are equivalent: x is a unit of R_Ψ; ψ(x) ∈ O^× for some ψ ∈ Ψ; ψ(x) ∈ O^× for every ψ ∈ Ψ. The reason is the congruence ψ(x) ≡ ψ′(x) mod 𝔪_O for x ∈ O[G] and ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ_χ.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.isUnit_iff_exists`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- Ψ is nonempty: for Ψ = ∅ the ring R_∅ is zero, every element of it is a unit, and there is no character.
- What is used: O is a local ring whose residue field has characteristic p, and for ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ the character ψ′ψ^{-1} has p-power order (it is trivial on G′, so it factors through the p-group G_p).

Construction or proof route:

- For ψ, ψ′ ∈ Ψ_χ the character ψ′ψ^{-1} is trivial on G′, so its values are p-power roots of unity of O. A p-power root of unity ζ of O is ≡ 1 mod 𝔪_O: its image ζ̄ in the residue field k, of characteristic p, satisfies ζ̄^{p^n} = 1, hence ζ̄ = 1 (ExpChar.pow_prime_pow_mul_eq_one_iff with m = 1).
- Hence for x = Σ_g a_g g ∈ O[G], ψ′(x) − ψ(x) = Σ_g a_g ψ(g)((ψ′ψ^{-1})(g) − 1) ∈ 𝔪_O. In the local ring O an element congruent modulo 𝔪_O to a unit is a unit, so ψ(x) ∈ O^× iff ψ′(x) ∈ O^×.
- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-criterion, x is a unit of R_Ψ iff every ψ(x), ψ ∈ Ψ, is a unit; by the previous step and Ψ ≠ ∅ this holds iff one of them is.

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring
- mathlib:ExpChar.pow_prime_pow_mul_eq_one_iff
- mathlib:HasEnoughRootsOfUnity
- mathlib:Monoid.exponent

Acceptance controls:

- G = C_p, Ψ = Ĝ, x = Σ_i a_i g^i ∈ O[C_p]: x is a unit iff the augmentation Σ_i a_i is a unit of O.
- Across two components one unit value does not suffice: for G = G′ = C_2 = {1, h} and p odd, the element (1 + h)/2 has value 1 at the trivial character and 0 at the sign character, and it is not a unit.

Source locators:

- DK-arXiv-v3 — §5.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34. The source uses, for R = O[G_p]_χ and one character ψ belonging to χ, that ψ(x) ∈ O^× implies x ∈ R^×; its only justification is the remark of §5.1 that the maps R → O are local homomorphisms of local rings.

#### Character group rings of one component are local

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local** — theorem.

For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ (for instance R_χ itself, or R_χ/N_I for a nontrivial subgroup I ⊆ G_p), R_Ψ is a local ring, and its maximal ideal is 𝔪_Ψ = {x ∈ R_Ψ : ψ(x) ∈ 𝔪_O}, for any ψ ∈ Ψ.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.isLocalRing`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- The two instances are nonempty. The character g′g_p ↦ χ(g′) of G = G_p × G′ lies in Ψ_χ. For a nontrivial subgroup I ⊆ G_p some character ψ_p of G_p is nontrivial on I (CommGroup.exists_apply_ne_one_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity for G_p, whose exponent divides that of G), and g′g_p ↦ χ(g′)ψ_p(g_p) lies in Ψ_χ and is nontrivial on I.

Construction or proof route:

- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character, for every ψ ∈ Ψ an element x ∈ R_Ψ is a unit iff ψ(x) ∈ O^×. So the set of non-units of R_Ψ is 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O): it does not depend on ψ, and it is the kernel of the ring homomorphism R_Ψ → O → k, hence an ideal.
- R_Ψ ≠ 0 because Ψ ≠ ∅ and O ≠ 0. A nonzero ring whose non-units are closed under addition is local (IsLocalRing.of_nonunits_add), and its maximal ideal is the set of non-units, here 𝔪_Ψ.

Immediate prerequisites:

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring
- mathlib:IsLocalRing
- mathlib:IsLocalRing.of_nonunits_add
- mathlib:CommGroup.exists_apply_ne_one_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity
- mathlib:HasEnoughRootsOfUnity
- mathlib:Monoid.exponent

Acceptance controls:

- Ψ = Ψ_1 for G = G_p: R_Ψ = O[G_p] is local, and its maximal ideal is the preimage of 𝔪_O under the augmentation.
- Ψ spanning two components (χ ≠ χ′) gives R_Ψ ≅ R_{Ψ∩Ψ_χ} × R_{Ψ∩Ψ_χ′}, which is not local.
- Ψ = ∅ is excluded: R_∅ = 0 is not a local ring.

Source locators:

- DK-arXiv-v3 — §2.2, arXiv v3 PDF p. 15. The source asserts without proof that each component R_χ = O[G_p]_χ is local; this is the case Ψ = Ψ_χ of the theorem.
- DK-arXiv-v3 — §5.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 34. The source treats R = O[G_p]_χ as a local ring here; that each character induces a local homomorphism R → O is the separate lemma on the evaluations.
- DK-arXiv-v3 — §7.2.9, arXiv v3 PDF p. 49. Stated without proof. In §7.2.9 the letter Ψ is not an arbitrary set of characters: from the end of §7.1 on, R denotes R_Ψ for the trivial-zero-free set Ψ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ, ψ(v) ≠ 1 for all v ∈ Σ}, a subset of the characters belonging to one χ. The theorem proves locality for every nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ. Nonemptiness is needed (R_∅ = 0 is not local) and is left implicit in the source; for a Ψ meeting two components R_Ψ is not local.
- DK-arXiv-v3 — §7.1, arXiv v3 PDF p. 43. Fixes what R = R_Ψ means in §7.2.9: the trivial-zero-free character group ring quotient of the component O[G_p]_χ.

#### A power of the maximal ideal of a character group ring lies in 𝔪_O R_Ψ

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-maximal-ideal-power** — lemma.

For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ, let 𝔪_Ψ be the maximal ideal of the local ring R_Ψ. Then 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ, and there is N ≥ 1 with 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ. Hence the powers of 𝔪_Ψ and of 𝔪_O R_Ψ define the same topology on R_Ψ.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.exists_maximalIdeal_pow_le`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- What is used: O is a local ring, R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module, and 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O) for the O-linear evaluation ev_ψ. Completeness of O is not used.
- The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local); the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module.

Construction or proof route:

- 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ: for a ∈ 𝔪_O and y ∈ R_Ψ, ev_ψ(a·y) = a·ev_ψ(y) ∈ 𝔪_O, and 𝔪_Ψ = ev_ψ^{-1}(𝔪_O) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local).
- A = R_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ is a finite module over the field k = O/𝔪_O, because R_Ψ is a finite O-module (it is a quotient of O[G]); hence A is an artinian ring (IsArtinianRing.of_finite). It is a local ring, as a quotient of the local ring R_Ψ by a proper ideal, with maximal ideal 𝔪_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ, and this is its Jacobson radical (IsLocalRing.jacobson_eq_maximalIdeal for the zero ideal).
- The Jacobson radical of an artinian ring is nilpotent (IsArtinianRing.isNilpotent_jacobson_bot): (𝔪_Ψ/𝔪_O R_Ψ)^N = 0 for some N, which can be taken ≥ 1. That is, 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ. Consequently (𝔪_O R_Ψ)^n ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ^n and 𝔪_Ψ^{Nn} ⊆ (𝔪_O R_Ψ)^n for every n.

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring

- mathlib:IsArtinianRing.isNilpotent_jacobson_bot

- G = G_p = C_p, Ψ = Ĝ: 𝔪_Ψ = (π, g − 1) with π a uniformiser of O, and (g − 1)^p ≡ g^p − 1 = 0 modulo p, so N = p works.
- The exponent depends on G: for O = Z_p and G = C_{p^n}, O[G]/pO[G] = F_p[x]/(x − 1)^{p^n}, and the least N is p^n.
- p ∤ #G: Ψ = {χ}, R_Ψ = O, 𝔪_Ψ = 𝔪_O and N = 1.

#### The evaluations of a character group ring of one component are local homomorphisms

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-eval-local-hom** — lemma.

For χ ∈ Ĝ′, a subset Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ = {ψ ∈ Ĝ : ψ|_{G′} = χ} and ψ ∈ Ψ, the evaluation ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is a local homomorphism: if ev_ψ(x) is a unit of O, then x is a unit of R_Ψ. Since R_Ψ and O are local rings, this says ev_ψ(𝔪_Ψ) ⊆ 𝔪_O.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.isLocalHom_eval`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- Ψ is nonempty because it contains ψ. A local homomorphism is one that reflects units (Mathlib's IsLocalHom); the locality of R_Ψ is not used in the proof.

Construction or proof route:

- Let x ∈ R_Ψ with ev_ψ(x) ∈ O^×. By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-unit-one-character, applied to the nonempty set Ψ and its element ψ, x is a unit of R_Ψ. This is the defining property of IsLocalHom for the homomorphism ev_ψ (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.eval).

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring
- mathlib:IsLocalHom
- mathlib:HasEnoughRootsOfUnity
- mathlib:Monoid.exponent

- The restriction to one component is needed: for G = G′ = C_2 = {1, h}, p odd and Ψ = Ĝ, the evaluation at the trivial character sends (1 + h)/2 to 1, and (1 + h)/2 is not a unit of R_Ĝ = O[G] (its value at the sign character is 0).

#### The residue field of a character group ring of one component

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-residue-field** — lemma.

For χ ∈ Ĝ′, a subset Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ and ψ ∈ Ψ, the homomorphism of residue fields R_Ψ/𝔪_Ψ → O/𝔪_O = k induced by the local homomorphism ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is bijective. So the residue field of the local ring R_Ψ is k.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.bijective_residueFieldMap_eval`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- R_Ψ is a local ring by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local, and ev_ψ is a local homomorphism by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-eval-local-hom; the induced map of residue fields is IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map.
- The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local) and through PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-eval-local-hom; the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring, a finite O-module, and ev_ψ is a local homomorphism.

Construction or proof route:

- The induced map R_Ψ/𝔪_Ψ → k is a homomorphism of fields, hence injective.
- It is surjective: it sends the class of x to the class of ev_ψ(x) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField.map_residue), ev_ψ : R_Ψ → O is surjective (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.eval_surjective), and O → k is surjective.

- p ∤ #G: Ψ = {χ}, R_Ψ ≅ O through ev_χ and the map is the identity of k.

These elements lie in 𝔪_Ψ (ev_ψ sends α_Ψ(g) − χ(g′) to χ(g′)(ψ(g_p) − 1) ∈ 𝔪_O), and the quotient of R_Ψ by them is a quotient of k[G]/(g − χ̄(g′) : g ∈ G) = k that maps onto k.

#### Character group rings of one component are complete noetherian local rings

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-adic-complete** — theorem.

For χ ∈ Ĝ′ and nonempty Ψ ⊆ Ψ_χ, the local ring R_Ψ is noetherian, and it is complete and separated for the 𝔪_Ψ-adic topology, which coincides with its 𝔪_O-adic topology because 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ for some N ≥ 1 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-maximal-ideal-power). So R_Ψ is a complete noetherian local O-algebra.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.isAdicComplete`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- What is used beyond locality: O is a noetherian local ring that is 𝔪_O-adically complete and separated, and R_Ψ is a finite O-module.
- The hypothesis on Ψ enters only through the locality of R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local); the statement holds for every Ψ for which R_Ψ is a local ring and a finite O-module.

Construction or proof route:

- R_Ψ is a finite O-module (a finite free one by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-lattice) and O is noetherian, so R_Ψ is a noetherian ring (IsNoetherianRing.of_finite).
- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-maximal-ideal-power, 𝔪_Ψ^N ⊆ 𝔪_O R_Ψ ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ for some N ≥ 1; here 𝔪_Ψ is the maximal ideal of the local ring R_Ψ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-local).
- R_Ψ is 𝔪_O-adically complete and separated as an O-module. Separated: R_Ψ is a finite module over the noetherian local ring O (IsHausdorff.of_isLocalRing, the Krull intersection theorem). Precomplete: by AdicCompletion.of_surjective_iff it suffices that the canonical map of : R_Ψ → AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ is surjective. The map AdicCompletion 𝔪_O O ⊗_O R_Ψ → AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ, r ⊗ x ↦ r·of(x) (AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct), is surjective because R_Ψ is a finite O-module (AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_surjective_of_finite), and every r ∈ AdicCompletion 𝔪_O O is of(a) with a ∈ O because O is complete (AdicCompletion.of_surjective_iff for O); since of(a)·of(x) = of(a·x), every element of AdicCompletion 𝔪_O R_Ψ is of(y) with y ∈ R_Ψ.
- From the O-module to the ring: by IsAdicComplete.map_algebraMap_iff, R_Ψ is complete and separated as a module over itself for the ideal J = 𝔪_O R_Ψ.
- From J to 𝔪_Ψ: J^n ⊆ 𝔪_Ψ^n and 𝔪_Ψ^{Nn} ⊆ J^n for all n, so the J-adic topology of R_Ψ is also 𝔪_Ψ-adic (isAdic_iff: the powers of 𝔪_Ψ are open and every neighbourhood of 0 contains one of them). Completeness and separatedness of an adic ring depend only on its topology (IsAdic.isAdicComplete_iff, applied to J and to 𝔪_Ψ), so R_Ψ is 𝔪_Ψ-adically complete and separated.

#### The order of a principal quotient of a character group ring

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-index** — theorem.

(Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.5.) For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ and a non-zerodivisor x ∈ R_Ψ, the quotient R_Ψ/xR_Ψ is finite and #(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O/(∏_{ψ∈Ψ} ψ(x))).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.card_quotient_span`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- What is used: O is a Dedekind domain (a discrete valuation ring) that is infinite (characteristic zero), #G ≠ 0 in O, and O/(a) is finite for every a ≠ 0; G is finite. The last condition is Ring.HasFiniteQuotients O. That class has no instance for a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field in the pinned Mathlib (only for finite rings, ℤ and rings of integers of number fields), so in the Dasgupta–Kakde setting it is derived as in the second proof step.

Construction or proof route:

- R_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ := ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O has finite index (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-finite-index), and x is a non-zerodivisor of O_Ψ with every ψ(x) ≠ 0 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-nonzerodivisor).
- O_Ψ/xO_Ψ = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} O/(ψ(x)) is finite, because every ψ(x) is nonzero and O/(a) is finite for a ≠ 0 (a nonzero ideal of the discrete valuation ring O is (ϖ^n) = 𝔪_O^n for a uniformiser ϖ, by IsDiscreteValuationRing.ideal_eq_span_pow_irreducible, and O/𝔪_O^n is finite by Ideal.finite_quotient_pow, because 𝔪_O is principal and the residue field O/𝔪_O is finite; this is Ring.HasFiniteQuotients O). Multiplication by x is an isomorphism O_Ψ/R_Ψ ≅ xO_Ψ/xR_Ψ, so [xO_Ψ : xR_Ψ] = [O_Ψ : R_Ψ] is finite. Multiplicativity of the index in the towers xR_Ψ ⊆ R_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ and xR_Ψ ⊆ xO_Ψ ⊆ O_Ψ (Submodule.card_quotient_mul_card_quotient) gives [O_Ψ : R_Ψ]·#(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ)·[xO_Ψ : xR_Ψ], and cancelling the equal finite nonzero factors gives #(R_Ψ/xR_Ψ) = #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ).
- #(O_Ψ/xO_Ψ) = ∏_{ψ∈Ψ} #(O/ψ(x)) = #(O/∏ψ(x)); the last equality is cardQuot_mul applied to the principal ideals (ψ(x)) of O, which is a Dedekind domain (a discrete valuation ring) and infinite (characteristic zero).

#### The involution # and the rings R^#

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/sharp-involution** — construction.

The involution # of O[G] is the O-algebra automorphism g ↦ g^{-1} (the antipode of the commutative Hopf algebra O[G]); (x^#)^# = x and ψ(x^#) = ψ^{-1}(x) for every character ψ. For Ψ ⊆ Ĝ put Ψ^# = Ψ^{-1} = {ψ^{-1} : ψ ∈ Ψ} and R^# = R_{Ψ^#} for R = R_Ψ. Then # maps ker α_Ψ onto ker α_{Ψ^#} and induces mutually inverse O-algebra isomorphisms # : R_Ψ → R_{Ψ^#} and # : R_{Ψ^#} → R_Ψ, with #(α_Ψ(x)) = α_{Ψ^#}(x^#) and (#y)(ψ^{-1}) = y(ψ). It is an endomorphism of R_Ψ only when Ψ^# = Ψ. For R = O[G] (and Z_p[G], Z[G]) R^# = R. Ideals transport as I^# = #(I) ⊆ R^#; in particular (xR)^# = x^#R^#.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.charGroupRing.sharpEquiv`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- Dasgupta–Kakde setting (§2.2): p is an odd prime; G is a finite abelian group, G = G_p × G′ with G_p its p-Sylow subgroup and G′ of order prime to p; O is the valuation ring of a finite extension K of Q_p, with finite residue field k, containing all values of all characters G → Q̄_p^×, that is, with enough roots of unity for the exponent e of G: HasEnoughRootsOfUnity O (Monoid.exponent G); Ĝ = Hom(G, O^×), a group of order #G (CommGroup.card_monoidHom_of_hasEnoughRootsOfUnity).
- The construction of # on O[G] needs only O commutative and G commutative.

Construction or proof route:

- # is HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgHom O O[G], for the Hopf algebra structure MonoidAlgebra.instHopfAlgebra of O[G] over O (the coefficient Hopf algebra is O itself); it is an algebra map because O[G] is commutative, G being commutative. MonoidAlgebra.antipode_single gives antipode(a·g) = antipode_O(a)·g^{-1}, and the antipode of O is the identity (CommSemiring.antipode_eq_id), so # sends a·g to a·g^{-1}; hence it agrees with MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainAlgHom of invMonoidHom. Involutivity (x^#)^# = x is TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.antipode_antipode, and # as a self-inverse automorphism is TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.antipodeAlgEquiv for A = O[G].
- ψ(g^#) = ψ(g^{-1}) = ψ(g)^{-1} = ψ^{-1}(g) on group elements (character-evaluation, TauCeti.charEval_of), hence on O[G] by linearity.
- Therefore x ∈ ker α_Ψ iff x^# ∈ ker α_{Ψ^#} (character-group-ring, TauCeti.charGroupRing.ker_proj). So α_{Ψ^#} ∘ # is surjective with kernel ker α_Ψ and factors through an isomorphism R_Ψ → R_{Ψ^#} (TauCeti.charGroupRing.lift); the same construction for Ψ^# gives its inverse, because # ∘ # = id and (Ψ^#)^# = Ψ.
- In the Dasgupta–Kakde setting ker α_Ψ determines Ψ: for ψ′ ∈ Ĝ ∖ Ψ the element e = Σ_g ψ′(g)^{-1} g has ψ(e) = 0 for every character ψ ≠ ψ′ and ψ′(e) = #G ≠ 0 (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/character-group-ring-scaled-idempotent for the set Ĝ and its element ψ′); so e lies in ker α_Ψ, and Ψ is the set of characters vanishing on ker α_Ψ. If # maps ker α_Ψ into itself, then ker α_{Ψ^#} = #(ker α_Ψ) ⊆ ker α_Ψ by the previous step, so Ψ ⊆ Ψ^#, and applying ψ ↦ ψ^{-1} gives Ψ^# ⊆ Ψ. Hence # maps ker α_Ψ into itself only when Ψ^# = Ψ.

#### The contragredient dual

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/contragredient-dual** — construction.

For a ring isomorphism σ : S → R of commutative rings (σ = # : R^# → R for R = R_Ψ, or # : R → R for R = O[G], Z_p[G], Z[G]) and an R-module M, the contragredient dual M^* = Hom_R(M, R) is the S-module with (s·φ)(x) = φ(σ(s)·x); for R = R_Ψ this is Dasgupta–Kakde's rule (r·φ)(x) = φ(r^#·x). A linear map f : M → N induces the S-linear f^* : N^* → M^*, φ ↦ φ∘f, functorially; for M = R^m, M^* is free over S on the dual basis.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.ContragredientDual`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R and S are commutative rings and σ is a ring isomorphism; the module structure is Module.compHom along σ.
- The source states the rule for Z[G]-modules, with M^* = Hom_{Z[G]}(M, Z[G]), and applies it to modules over a character group ring R = R_Ψ. For an R-module the dual is Hom_R(M, R), the reading that Lemma 6.1 requires. The general form, with a ring isomorphism σ : S → R, covers both.

Construction or proof route:

- Give Module.Dual R M the S-module structure Module.compHom along σ; (s·φ)(x) = σ(s)φ(x) = φ(σ(s)x) by R-linearity of φ.
- f^* is LinearMap.dualMap f, φ ↦ φ∘f, which is S-linear for the transported structures; the identity and composition laws hold for dualMap.
- For M = R^m the dual basis identifies M^* with R^m (Module.piEquiv with values in R), and σ^{-1} coordinatewise identifies it with S^m: φ ↦ (σ^{-1}(φ(e_i)))_i, which is S-linear because σ^{-1}(σ(s)·φ(e_i)) = s·σ^{-1}(φ(e_i)). For an m×n matrix A, (φ∘A)(e_j) = Σ_i A_{ij}·φ(e_i), so the dual of A becomes the n×m matrix with (j, i) entry σ^{-1}(A_{ij}).
- Semilinear form: for φ ∈ M^* the map σ^{-1}∘φ : M → S is additive and σ^{-1}-semilinear, an element of Mathlib's S-module of semilinear maps (LinearMap along the ring homomorphism σ^{-1}); φ ↦ σ^{-1}∘φ is bijective with inverse ψ ↦ σ∘ψ, and σ^{-1}((s·φ)(x)) = s·σ^{-1}(φ(x)), so it is S-linear for the pointwise structure.
- Group rings: for a finite commutative group G, R = S = O[G] and σ = #, the map Ψ : Hom_O(M, O) → M^*, Ψ_f(m) = Σ_{g∈G} f(g·m)·g^{-1}, takes values in O[G]-linear maps (Ψ_f(h·m) = h·Ψ_f(m)), has inverse φ ↦ (the coefficient of 1 in φ(·)), and satisfies Ψ_{f∘h^{-1}} = h·Ψ_f for h ∈ G; so the action of G on M^* corresponds to Mathlib's dual representation Representation.dual.
- Products and projectivity: Module.dualProdDualEquivDual, (φ, ψ) ↦ φ∘fst + ψ∘snd, is S-linear for the contragredient structures, since s acts on all three duals as σ(s). If M is a finitely generated projective R-module, Module.Dual R M is finitely generated and projective over R (Module.dual_finite, Module.dual_projective). The bijection toDual : M^* → Module.Dual R M is σ-semilinear, so M^* is projective over S (Module.Projective.of_equiv, with σ and σ^{-1} as the two mutually inverse ring homomorphisms), and a finite generating set of Module.Dual R M over R generates M^* over S because σ is surjective.

#### Quadratically presented modules

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation** — definition.

Let R be a commutative ring. A quadratic presentation of an R-module N consists of an integer m ≥ 1, an m×m matrix φ over R and a surjection π : R^m → N whose kernel is the image of φ : R^m → R^m; N is quadratically presented over R if it has one, equivalently N ≅ coker(φ) for a square matrix φ of size m ≥ 1.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.QuadraticPresentation`.

Atlas planet: Quadratically presented module.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- m ≥ 1 is part of the definition (the zero module is presented by R →(1) R).

Construction or proof route:

- Record (m, φ, π) with π surjective and range(φ) = ker(π). The Mathlib presentation with generators and relations indexed by Fin m (the j-th relation is the j-th column of φ, the i-th variable is π(e_i)) is a presentation by Module.Relations.Solution.isPresentation_iff, so a quadratically presented module is finitely presented (Module.Presentation.finitePresentation).
- Base change: R′ ⊗_R − applied to the exact sequence R^m → R^m → N → 0 gives an exact sequence whose last map is surjective (lTensor_exact, the right exactness of the tensor product); under R′ ⊗_R R^m ≅ R′^m its first map is the image matrix.
- Direct sums use the block-diagonal matrix, of size m + m′ and determinant det φ·det φ′ (Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁ with zero upper-right block); transport along an isomorphism composes π and keeps the matrix (Module.Presentation.ofLinearEquiv on the Mathlib side); coker(φ) is presented by φ and the quotient map (compare Module.Presentation.cokernel). Mathlib has no base change of a Module.Presentation along a ring map at the pin, so base change is built here.
- The isomorphism R^m/φR^m ≅ N: π induces R^m/ker π ≅ N (LinearMap.quotKerEquivOfSurjective), and ker π = range φ. Together with cokernel and ofLinearEquiv this is the equivalence with N ≅ coker(φ) in the statement.

Semantic unit tests:

- quadratic_cyclic (computation): R/(a) has a quadratic presentation of size 1 with determinant a.
- quadratic_zero (degenerate): The zero module is quadratically presented (m = 1, φ = (1)); m = 0 is excluded.
- quadratic_free (degenerate): R^m (m ≥ 1) has a quadratic presentation with φ = 0.
- not_quadratic_residue_field (non-example): Over R = Z_p⟦T⟧ the module R/(p, T) is not quadratically presented. R is a noetherian domain and its maximal ideal (p, T) has height 2 (0 ⊂ (T) ⊂ (p, T)), so the module vanishes after localising at (0) and at every height-one prime. If it were coker(φ) for a square matrix φ, then φ would be surjective, hence invertible, after each of these localisations, so det φ would be a nonzero element lying in no height-one prime, hence a unit (a minimal prime over a nonzero non-unit of a noetherian domain has height one: Krull's principal ideal theorem), and coker(φ) would be 0.
- quadratic_baseChange (computation): For a ring homomorphism R → R′ and a ∈ R, the base change of the presentation R →(a) R of R/(a) is a quadratic presentation of R′ ⊗_R R/(a) over R′ of size 1 whose matrix is (a′), a′ the image of a in R′.
- quadratic_toPresentation (compatibility): For a quadratic presentation P = (m, φ, π), the Mathlib presentation P.toPresentation has generators and relations indexed by Fin m, its i-th variable is π(e_i) and the i-th coefficient of its j-th relation is φ_{ij}.
- quadratic_columns (computation): φ = [[0, 1], [0, 0]] over a nontrivial ring R: e_1 lies in the image of φ and e_2 does not, so in coker(φ) = R²/φR² the class of e_1 is 0 and the class of e_2 is not 0. The relations are the columns of φ (the image of φ acting on column vectors), not its rows.

#### The Fitting ideal of a quadratic presentation

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-quadratic** — theorem.

If N has a quadratic presentation R^m →φ R^m → N → 0, then Fitt_R(N) = (det φ); in particular Fitt_R(N) is principal.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.QuadraticPresentation.fittingIdeal_eq`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).

Construction or proof route:

- N is finitely presented (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation), and (π, φ) is a finite presentation with m generators. By presentation independence of the imported Fitting ideal, Fitt_R(N) is generated by the m×m minors of φ.
- The only m×m minor of the m×m matrix φ is det φ.

- N = R^m: Fitt = (det 0) = 0 for m ≥ 1.

#### Higher Fitting ideals of a finitely presented module

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal** — definition.

Let R be a commutative ring, M a finitely presented R-module and i ≥ 0 an integer. For elements x_1, …, x_n of M with relation module K(x) = {r ∈ R^n : Σ_j r_j·x_j = 0} and for k ≥ 0, let J_k(x) be the ideal of R generated by the minors of size k of all n×k matrices whose columns lie in K(x) (J_0(x) = R); the relation-minors ideal of x in degree i is J_{n−i}(x) for i ≤ n and R for i > n. The i-th Fitting ideal Fitt^i_R(M) is the sum of the relation-minors ideals in degree i of all finite generating families of M. Every generating family gives the whole ideal (API item TauCeti.Module.higherFittingIdeal_eq_relationMinorsIdeal), so that for a finite presentation R^m →A R^n →π M → 0 (π surjective, the columns of the n×m matrix A generating ker π) Fitt^i_R(M) is the ideal generated by the minors of A of size n − i, that is the determinants of the (n − i)×(n − i) submatrices of A, when i < n, and Fitt^i_R(M) = R when i ≥ n. For i = 0 it is the imported initial Fitting ideal Fitt_R(M).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.Module.higherFittingIdeal`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- M is finitely presented, as in the source (Appendix B.2: ‘finitely presented R-module M’).
- Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).
- The minor of size 0 is 1, the determinant of the empty matrix, so Fitt^n_R(M) = R is the case of minors of size 0, and Fitt^i_R(M) = R for i > n continues the chain; when n − i exceeds the number m of relations there is no minor and the ideal is 0.
- The sum over all generating families is a definition without choices. That one family, or one presentation matrix, already gives the whole ideal is the independence theorem (API items higherFittingIdeal_eq_relationMinorsIdeal and higherFittingIdeal_eq_span_minors); the comparison of Fitt^0 with the imported ideal, base change and localisation follow from it (higherFittingIdeal_zero, higherFittingIdeal_baseChange, higherFittingIdeal_localization). Each is proved in its own node; the proof steps below use none of them.

Construction or proof route:

- Matrix form of J_k. If the columns of an n×m matrix A generate K(x), then J_k(x) is the ideal of the k-minors of A: a matrix with columns in K(x) is A·V for some m×k matrix V, and its k-minors are combinations of k-minors of A by the Cauchy–Binet formula for the rectangular matrices A and V (Matrix.compound_mul of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/compound-matrix); conversely a k-minor of A is a minor of the matrix formed by k of its columns. For a generating family of a finitely presented module a finite such A exists (Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker).
- J_{k+1}(x) ⊆ J_k(x): by Laplace expansion along a row (Matrix.det_succ_row) a (k + 1)-minor is a combination of k-minors of the matrix obtained by deleting a column, whose columns still lie in K(x). In degrees: the relation-minors ideal in degree i is contained in the one in degree i + 1.
- Chain and top degree: summing step 2 over the finite generating families gives Fitt^i_R(M) ⊆ Fitt^{i+1}_R(M). If M has a generating family with n elements and i ≥ n, the term of that family is R, so Fitt^i_R(M) = R.
- Monotonicity: for a surjection f : M → M′ of finitely presented modules and a generating family x of M, the family f(x_1), …, f(x_n) generates M′ and K(x) ⊆ K(f(x)), so J_k(x) ⊆ J_k(f(x)) for all k; summing over the families gives Fitt^i_R(M) ⊆ Fitt^i_R(M′). Applied to an isomorphism and its inverse: isomorphic modules have equal Fitting ideals.

#### A redundant generator shifts the ideals of relation minors

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/relation-minors-add-generator** — lemma.

Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, x_1, …, x_n ∈ M and y = Σ_i c_i·x_i with c_i ∈ R; put x′ = (x_1, …, x_n, y). With J_k as in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal (the ideal generated by the k-minors of the matrices with k columns that are relations among the family), J_k(x′) = J_{k−1}(x) for every k ≥ 1. Equivalently x′ and x have the same relation-minors ideal in every degree i ≥ 0: J_{n+1−i}(x′) = J_{n−i}(x) for i ≤ n, and both are R for i > n.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.Module.relationMinorsIdeal_snoc`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- M is any R-module and x any finite family, possibly empty; x need not generate M. Only y ∈ Σ_i R·x_i is used.
- For k = 0 both J_0(x′) and J_0(x) are R; this is the degree i = n + 1, where the family x has more degree than elements.

Construction or proof route:

- Let K ⊆ R^n and K′ ⊆ R^{n+1} be the relation modules of x and x′. The matrix T with T(r, s) = (r + s·c, s) is invertible, with inverse (r, s) ↦ (r − s·c, s), and maps K′ onto K × R, because Σ_i r_i·x_i + s·y = Σ_i (r_i + s·c_i)·x_i.
- For an (n + 1)×k matrix B′ with columns in K′, the k-minors of T·B′ are combinations of the k-minors of B′ by the Cauchy–Binet formula (Matrix.compound_mul of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/compound-matrix), and conversely with T^{-1}. So J_k(x′) is the ideal generated by the k-minors of the (n + 1)×k matrices with columns in K × R.
- A k-minor of such a matrix either avoids the last row, and is a k-minor of an n×k matrix with columns in K, an element of J_k(x); or contains it, and is by expansion along that row (Matrix.det_succ_row) a combination of (k − 1)-minors of matrices with columns in K, an element of J_{k−1}(x). Every generator of J_{k−1}(x) occurs: border an n×(k − 1) matrix with columns in K by the column (0, 1) ∈ K × R and take the minor on the chosen rows and the last row.
- J_k(x) ⊆ J_{k−1}(x) (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal, relationMinorsIdeal_le_succ). Hence J_k(x′) = J_{k−1}(x) for k ≥ 1; with k = n + 1 − i this is the degree form for i ≤ n.

Immediate prerequisites:

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/compound-matrix
- mathlib:Matrix.det_succ_row

Acceptance controls:

- M = Z/3, x = (1), y = 1 (c = 1): K = 3Z and K′ = {(r, s) : r + s ∈ 3Z} is spanned by (3, 0) and (−1, 1). J_1(x′) = (3, −1, 0, 1) = Z = J_0(x) and J_2(x′) = (det [[3, −1], [0, 1]]) = (3) = J_1(x).
- x empty (n = 0) and y = 0: K′ = R, J_1(x′) = R = J_0(x). This is why the zero module has Fitt^0 = R whether it is generated by no element or by the element 0.
- In general, if the columns of A span K, the columns of [[A, −c], [0, 1]] span K′, and the ideal of its k-minors is the ideal of the (k − 1)-minors of A; for A = diag(2, 4) and c = (0, 1) the matrix [[2, 0, 0], [0, 4, −1], [0, 0, 1]] has minors of sizes 3, 2, 1 generating (8), (2), Z.

- DK-arXiv-v3 — Appendix B.2, the paragraph before Lemma B.5, arXiv v3 PDF p. 94. The source computes Fitt^s ‘by definition’ from one presentation matrix and does not prove that the ideal of minors is independent of the presentation. This lemma is the step of the standard proof that compares two generating families differing by one redundant generator; it is supplied here and no further source was read for it.

#### Higher Fitting ideals do not depend on the presentation

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-independence** — theorem.

Let R be a commutative ring, M a finitely presented R-module and i ≥ 0. For every finite generating family x_1, …, x_n of M, Fitt^i_R(M) is the relation-minors ideal of x in degree i, that is J_{n−i}(x) for i ≤ n and R for i > n (notation of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal). In matrix form: for every finite presentation R^m →A R^n →π M → 0 (π surjective, the columns of the n×m matrix A generating ker π), Fitt^i_R(M) is the ideal generated by the minors of A of size n − i (R when i ≥ n, 0 when n − i > m). In particular Fitt^0_R(M) is the imported initial Fitting ideal Fitt_R(M).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.Module.higherFittingIdeal_eq_relationMinorsIdeal`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- M is finitely presented, as in the source (Appendix B.2: ‘finitely presented R-module M’). The comparison of two generating families uses only that both generate M.
- Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).
- Fitt^i_R(M) is the higher Fitting ideal of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal: the sum, over all finite generating families of M, of their relation-minors ideals in degree i.

Construction or proof route:

- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/relation-minors-add-generator the relation-minors ideal of a family in degree i does not change when an element of the span of the family is appended.
- Let x (n elements) and y (p elements) be finite generating families of M. Appending y_1, …, y_p to x one at a time, each a combination of x, and x_1, …, x_n to y, gives the same relation-minors ideals for x and (x, y), and for y and (y, x). The families (x, y) and (y, x) differ by a permutation of coordinates, which permutes the relation modules and changes minors by signs. So x and y have the same relation-minors ideal in every degree.
- Fitt^i_R(M) is the sum of these ideals over all finite generating families (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal); they are all equal, and one exists because M is finitely generated. Hence Fitt^i_R(M) is the relation-minors ideal of any one of them.
- Matrix form: for x_j = π(e_j) the columns of A generate K(x) = ker π, so J_{n−i}(x) is the ideal of the (n − i)-minors of A (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal, relationMinorsIdeal_eq_span_minors); for n − i > m there is no such minor.
- i = 0: J_n(x) is the ideal of the n×n minors of a relation matrix, which is the definition of the imported Fitt_R(M); so Fitt^0_R(M) = Fitt_R(M).
- Examples: R^n is presented by n generators and no relation, so its ideal of k-minors is 0 for k ≥ 1 and R for k = 0. R/(a) is presented by the 1×1 matrix (a). R/(a) ⊕ R/(b) is presented by diag(a, b), whose 2-minor is ab and whose 1-minors are a, 0, 0, b.

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/relation-minors-add-generator
- tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs
- mathlib:Module.FinitePresentation

- Z/2 ⊕ Z/4 over Z from diag(2, 4) and from the three-generator presentation [[2, 0, 0], [0, 4, −1], [0, 0, 1]]: both give Fitt^0 = (8), Fitt^1 = (2), Fitt^2 = Z.
- The rule matters: with minors of size m − i, m the number of relations, the two presentations of Z/3 by (3, 9) and by [[3, 0], [0, 1]] would give 0, (3), Z and (3), Z, Z.

That the ideal of minors does not depend on the presentation is the standard theorem behind this; it is not stated or proved in the source. The proof given here is the standard one, and no further source was read for it.

#### Higher Fitting ideals commute with base change and localisation

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-base-change** — lemma.

Let R → R′ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, M a finitely presented R-module and i ≥ 0. Then R′ ⊗_R M is a finitely presented R′-module and Fitt^i_{R′}(R′ ⊗_R M) = Fitt^i_R(M)·R′, the ideal of R′ generated by the image of Fitt^i_R(M). In particular, for a multiplicative subset S of R, Fitt^i_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M) = S^{-1}Fitt^i_R(M).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.Module.higherFittingIdeal_baseChange`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- R → R′ is an arbitrary ring homomorphism; no flatness is assumed.
- Fitt^i is the higher Fitting ideal of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal; for i = 0 the statement is the base change of the imported carrier.

Construction or proof route:

- Choose a finite presentation R^m →A R^n →π M → 0 (Module.FinitePresentation.fg_ker). Applying R′ ⊗_R − gives an exact sequence R′ ⊗_R R^m → R′ ⊗_R R^n → R′ ⊗_R M → 0 whose last map is surjective (lTensor_exact, the right exactness of the tensor product), and under R′ ⊗_R R^k ≅ R′^k its first map is the matrix A′ obtained by applying R → R′ to the entries of A. So R′ ⊗_R M is finitely presented, with n generators and relation matrix A′.
- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-independence, Fitt^i_R(M) is generated by the (n − i)-minors of A and Fitt^i_{R′}(R′ ⊗_R M) by the (n − i)-minors of A′ (both are the unit ideal for i ≥ n). A minor of A′ is the image of the corresponding minor of A (RingHom.map_det). Hence Fitt^i_{R′}(R′ ⊗_R M) = Fitt^i_R(M)·R′.
- Localisation is the case R′ = S^{-1}R: S^{-1}M ≅ S^{-1}R ⊗_R M as S^{-1}R-modules (LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct), and isomorphic modules have the same Fitting ideals (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-ideal, higherFittingIdeal_eq_of_linearEquiv).

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/higher-fitting-independence

- mathlib:RingHom.map_det
- mathlib:LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct

- Z → Q and M = Z ⊕ Z/2: Q ⊗ M = Q has Fitting ideals 0, Q; these are the extensions of 0 and (2).
- R → R/I and M = R/(a): (R/I) ⊗_R M = (R/I)/(ā) has Fitt^0 = (ā), the image of (a).

This uses that Fitting ideals commute with base change, which the source does not state. The lemma is standard; its proof is supplied here and no further source was read for it.

#### Locally quadratic presentations

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/locally-quadratic-presentation** — definition.

A locally quadratic presentation of an R-module M is an exact sequence P_1 →f P_0 →π M → 0 with P_0, P_1 finitely generated projective R-modules of the same constant rank r (rank of (P_i)_𝔭 equal to r at every prime 𝔭). Every quadratic presentation is locally quadratic. Over a ring with finitely many maximal ideals — for instance a local ring, or a finite product of local rings such as Z_p[G], O[G] and the character group rings R_Ψ — a module with a locally quadratic presentation is quadratically presented, because finitely generated projective modules of constant rank over such a ring are free (Dasgupta–Kakde Remark A.7, for Z_p[G]): for r ≥ 1 the presentation becomes R^r → R^r → M → 0 after a choice of bases, and for r = 0 the module M is 0, presented by R →(1) R. An arbitrary Z_p[G]-algebra is not a finite product of local rings (Z_p[G][X] has infinitely many maximal ideals), and over a general ring a locally quadratic presentation need not be quadratic: for a non-principal ideal I of a Dedekind domain R, I ↪ R ↠ R/I is locally quadratic of rank 1, but R/I is not quadratically presented. For the Z_p[G]-algebras R of Remark A.7 the presentation is the base change of the locally quadratic presentation over Z_p[G]; that one is quadratic, and its base change to R is quadratic by QuadraticPresentation.baseChange.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.IsLocallyQuadraticPresentation`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- Constant rank r means Module.rankAtStalk P 𝔭 = r for every prime 𝔭 of R, the rank of the free R_𝔭-module P_𝔭.

Construction or proof route:

- Over a local ring, a finitely generated projective module is flat (Module.Flat.of_projective), hence free (Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing); a free module has rank at every stalk equal to its rank (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_finrank_of_free), so it is free of rank r.
- More generally, over a ring R with finitely many maximal ideals a finitely generated projective module of constant rank r is free of rank r (Module.nonempty_basis_of_flat_of_finrank_eq, which asks that (R/𝔪) ⊗_R P have dimension r over R/𝔪 for every maximal ideal 𝔪. Module.rankAtStalk_eq gives the rank at 𝔪 as the dimension of κ(𝔪) ⊗_R P over κ(𝔪), the residue field of the local ring R_𝔪; κ(𝔪) ⊗_R P ≅ κ(𝔪) ⊗_{R/𝔪} ((R/𝔪) ⊗_R P) by TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, and its dimension over κ(𝔪) is the dimension of (R/𝔪) ⊗_R P over the field R/𝔪 by Module.finrank_baseChange). For R = ∏_i A_i with A_i local this is the factorwise statement: P = ∏_i P_i with P_i free over A_i of rank r (step 1 on each factor). Hence P_0 ≅ R^r ≅ P_1, and for r ≥ 1 the presentation becomes R^r → R^r → M → 0.
- For r = 0 the module P_0 has rank 0 at every prime, so P_0 = 0 (Module.rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton) and M = 0, which is quadratically presented by R →(1) R; this needs no hypothesis on R.
- A quadratic presentation has P_0 = P_1 = R^m, of constant rank m.
- Base change: for a ring map R → R′, tensoring is right exact (lTensor_exact) and preserves finitely generated projective modules and their ranks (Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange), so the base change of a locally quadratic presentation is locally quadratic, and the base change of a quadratic one is quadratic (QuadraticPresentation.baseChange of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation). This is how Remark A.7 passes from Z_p[G] to a Z_p[G]-algebra.

- TauCeti.IsLocallyQuadraticPresentation.baseChange (functoriality): For a ring map R → R′, the base change P_1 ⊗_R R′ → P_0 ⊗_R R′ → M ⊗_R R′ → 0 of a locally quadratic presentation is a locally quadratic presentation of the same rank.

Semantic unit tests:

- lq_quadratic (compatibility): A quadratic presentation (φ, π) is a locally quadratic presentation.
- lq_unequal_rank (non-example): R = Z_p × Z_p, I = Z_p × 0: the presentation I ↪ R ↠ R/I is not locally quadratic (ranks of I are 1 and 0).
- lq_rank_zero (degenerate): 0 → 0 → 0 → 0 is locally quadratic of rank 0.
- lq_not_quadratic (non-example): R = Z[√−5], I = (2, 1 + √−5): the presentation I ↪ R ↠ R/I is locally quadratic of rank 1 (I is an invertible ideal, hence projective of rank 1), but R/I is not quadratically presented: for a square presentation φ of R/I, comparing the lengths of the cokernel after localising at each prime (where R is a discrete valuation ring) gives (det φ) = I, whereas I is not principal (I has norm 2, and a² + 5b² = 2 has no integer solution). A locally quadratic presentation is quadratic over rings with finitely many maximal ideals, not in general.

#### Generators and relations of an extension with a quadratically presented quotient

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/extension-relation-matrix** — lemma.

Let R be a commutative ring and 0 → A → B → C → 0 an exact sequence of R-modules. Let a_1, …, a_n generate A, with relation matrix Ψ of size n×p (its columns generate the module K_A of relations among the a_i), and let C be quadratically presented by (m, φ_C, π_C), with lifts c̃_j ∈ B of the generators π_C(e_j). Let X be an n×m matrix with Σ_j (φ_C)_{jk}·c̃_j = Σ_i X_{ik}·a_i for every k (the k-th lifted relation of C written in the generators of A; such an X exists). Then a_1, …, a_n, c̃_1, …, c̃_m generate B, and the relations among them are generated by the columns of the block upper-triangular matrix [[Ψ, −X], [0, φ_C]] of size (n + m)×(p + m).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.range_toLin'_fromBlocks_eq_ker_of_exact`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- A is identified with its image in B. Ψ is any matrix whose columns generate the relations among a_1, …, a_n; p need not equal n (p = 0 is allowed), and A need not be quadratically presented.
- The proof shows more: without any finite Ψ, the module of relations among (a, c̃) is K_A × 0 plus the span of the m columns (−X_k, (φ_C)_k). So the lemma has a form for a finitely generated A whose relations are not finitely generated.
- Exactness is used at A (injectivity of A → B), at B, and at C (surjectivity of B → C, for the lifts c̃_j); of the presentation of C only range φ_C = ker π_C and the surjectivity of π_C are used.
- The sign of X comes from moving the lifted relation to the other side; replacing each a_i by −a_i turns −X into X.

Construction or proof route:

- Generation: for b ∈ B write the image of b in C as Σ_j y_j·π_C(e_j) (π_C is surjective). Then b − Σ_j y_j·c̃_j maps to 0 in C, so it lies in A (exactness at B) and is a combination of the a_i.
- X exists and the columns are relations: for each k, Σ_j (φ_C)_{jk}·c̃_j maps to π_C(φ_C e_k) = 0 in C, hence lies in A and equals Σ_i X_{ik}·a_i for some X_{ik}; so (−X_k, (φ_C)_k) is a relation among (a, c̃), and so is (x, 0) for every x ∈ K_A, in particular for every column of Ψ.
- Every relation is a combination of these: if Σ_i x_i·a_i + Σ_j y_j·c̃_j = 0 in B, applying B → C gives Σ_j y_j·π_C(e_j) = 0, so y = φ_C z for some z ∈ R^m (range φ_C = ker π_C). Then Σ_j y_j·c̃_j = Σ_i (Xz)_i·a_i, so Σ_i (x + Xz)_i·a_i = 0 in B, hence in A (A → B is injective), that is x + Xz ∈ K_A. Thus (x, y) = (x + Xz, 0) + (−Xz, φ_C z).
- The columns of Ψ generate K_A, so x + Xz = Ψw for some w ∈ R^p and (x, y) = (Ψw, 0) + (−Xz, φ_C z) is a combination of the columns of the block matrix.

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation

- A non-split extension with A not cyclic and a rectangular Ψ: R = Z, B = Z/2 ⊕ Z/8, a_1 = (1, 0), a_2 = (0, 2), so A ≅ Z/2 ⊕ Z/4, with Ψ = [[2, 0, 2, 0], [0, 4, 4, 8]]; C = B/A ≅ Z/2 with φ_C = (2) and c̃ = (0, 1). Then 2·c̃ = a_2 gives X = (0, 1)ᵀ and the 3×5 matrix [[2, 0, 2, 0, 0], [0, 4, 4, 8, −1], [0, 0, 0, 0, 2]], whose cokernel is Z/2 ⊕ Z/8 (Smith invariants 1, 2, 8), not A ⊕ C.
- No relations in A (p = 0): 0 → Z → Z → Z/2 → 0 with first map multiplication by 2, a = 2, c̃ = 1: X = (1) and the 2×1 matrix [[−1], [2]], with cokernel Z.
- 0 → R/(a) → R/(ab) → R/(b) → 0 for a non-zerodivisor b, the first map being multiplication by b: generators (b, 1) of R/(ab), lifted relation b·1 = 1·b, X = (1), matrix [[a, −1], [0, b]].

#### An extension of quadratically presented modules is quadratically presented

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation-extension** — theorem.

(Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.6, second assertion.) Let R be a commutative ring and 0 → A → B → C → 0 an exact sequence of R-modules with A quadratically presented by (n, ψ_A, π_A) and C quadratically presented by (m, φ_C, π_C). Then B is quadratically presented, of size n + m, by the block upper-triangular matrix [[ψ_A, −X], [0, φ_C]] and the generators a_1, …, a_n, c̃_1, …, c̃_m, where a_i = π_A(e_i), the c̃_j ∈ B are lifts of the π_C(e_j), and X is an n×m matrix with Σ_j (φ_C)_{jk}·c̃_j = Σ_i X_{ik}·a_i for every k. The determinant of this matrix is det ψ_A·det φ_C.

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.isQuadraticallyPresented_of_exact`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- A is identified with its image in B. The presentation of B depends on the choice of the lifts c̃_j and of X; its size n + m and its determinant det ψ_A·det φ_C do not.
- The sign of X comes from moving the lifted relation to the other side; it does not affect the determinant, and replacing each a_i by −a_i turns −X into X.

Construction or proof route:

- By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/extension-relation-matrix with Ψ = ψ_A (so p = n), the family a_1, …, a_n, c̃_1, …, c̃_m generates B and its relations are generated by the columns of [[ψ_A, −X], [0, φ_C]].
- This matrix is square of size n + m ≥ 1, so together with the surjection R^{n+m} → B it is a quadratic presentation of B (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation; as data, QuadraticPresentation.ofExact).
- Its determinant is det ψ_A·det φ_C (Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁).

#### Fitting ideals of extensions with a quadratically presented quotient

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-extension** — theorem.

(Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.6, first assertion.) Let R be a commutative ring and 0 → A → B → C → 0 an exact sequence of R-modules with C quadratically presented and A finitely presented. Then B is finitely presented and Fitt_R(B) = Fitt_R(A)·Fitt_R(C).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.fittingIdeal_eq_mul_of_exact`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).
- A finitely presented is needed for Fitt_R(A); then B is finitely presented, as an extension of finitely presented modules (Module.finitePresentation_of_ker). The source states the lemma for an arbitrary commutative ring and an arbitrary module A and leaves this implicit (in its applications the modules are finitely generated over noetherian rings) and fixes the convention in Appendix B.2 (‘finitely presented R-module M’).

Construction or proof route:

- Choose a finite presentation of A, with generators a_1, …, a_n and relation matrix Ψ of size n×p, and a quadratic presentation (m, φ_C, π_C) of C with lifts c̃_j ∈ B of its generators. By PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/extension-relation-matrix, B is generated by a_1, …, a_n, c̃_1, …, c̃_m with relation matrix the block matrix [[Ψ, −X], [0, φ_C]] of size (n + m)×(p + m). B is finitely presented by Module.finitePresentation_of_ker applied to B → C: C is finitely presented (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation) and the kernel is isomorphic to A.
- Fitt_R(B) is generated by the minors of size n + m of this matrix; such a minor selects all n + m rows and n + m of the columns. If it uses only j < m of the last m columns, the selected square matrix has an m×(n + m − j) block of zeros (the last m rows of the n + m − j columns taken from the first block) with m + (n + m − j) > n + m, so its determinant is 0: in the Leibniz expansion every permutation must send the last m rows into the j remaining columns.
- If it uses all of the last m columns and n of the first p, the selected matrix is [[U, −X], [0, φ_C]] with U the n×n matrix formed by n columns of Ψ, and its determinant is det(U)·det(φ_C) by Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁. The determinants det(U) generate Fitt_R(A), so Fitt_R(B) = Fitt_R(A)·(det φ_C) = Fitt_R(A)·Fitt_R(C) by PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-quadratic.

Immediate prerequisites:

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-quadratic
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/extension-relation-matrix
- tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs
- mathlib:Module.finitePresentation_of_ker
- mathlib:Matrix.det_fromBlocks_zero₂₁

Acceptance controls:

- 0 → R/(a) → R/(ab) → R/(b) → 0 for a non-zerodivisor b: (ab) = (a)(b).
- Split sequences B = A ⊕ C: Fitt(A ⊕ C) = Fitt(A)Fitt(C) when C is quadratically presented.
- The hypothesis on C cannot be dropped: for R = Z[x] and 𝔪 = (2, x), the sequence 0 → 𝔪/𝔪² → R/𝔪² → R/𝔪 → 0 has Fitt_R(B) = 𝔪², Fitt_R(A) = 𝔪² (A ≅ (R/𝔪)²) and Fitt_R(C) = 𝔪, and 𝔪² ≠ 𝔪³ because 4 ∉ 𝔪³; here C = R/𝔪 is not quadratically presented.

#### Fitting ideals of two extensions of a common quotient

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-fibre-product** — theorem.

(Dasgupta–Kakde Lemma 2.7.) Let B, B′ be quadratically presented R-modules with exact sequences 0 → A → B → C → 0 and 0 → A′ → B′ → C → 0, A and A′ finitely presented. Then Fitt_R(A)·Fitt_R(B′) = Fitt_R(A′)·Fitt_R(B).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.fittingIdeal_mul_comm_of_exact`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- R is an arbitrary commutative ring; no noetherian or finiteness hypothesis is made beyond the stated ones.
- Fitt_R(M) = Fitt^0_R(M) is the initial Fitting ideal of a finitely presented R-module M: the ideal generated by the n×n minors of the relation matrix of any finite presentation with n generators, independent of the presentation and compatible with base change. It is the finite-presentation Fitting-ideal carrier imported from the Tau Ceti roadmap StableReduction, Layer 1 (accepted RS-16).
- A and A′ are finitely presented; then the fibre product B ×_C B′ is finitely presented, as an extension of B by A′. The source leaves this implicit (its modules are finitely generated over noetherian rings, where A and A′ are automatically finitely presented) and fixes the convention in Appendix B.2.

Construction or proof route:

- Form M = B ×_C B′, the pairs (b, b′) with the same image in C.
- The first projection M → B is surjective because B′ → C is, with kernel {(0, b′) : b′ ↦ 0 in C} ≅ A′; the second projection M → B′ is surjective because B → C is, with kernel ≅ A. So 0 → A′ → M → B → 0 and 0 → A → M → B′ → 0 are exact.
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-extension applied to the first sequence (quotient B quadratically presented, kernel A′ finitely presented) gives Fitt_R(M) = Fitt_R(A′)·Fitt_R(B); applied to the second (quotient B′ quadratically presented, kernel A finitely presented) it gives Fitt_R(M) = Fitt_R(A)·Fitt_R(B′).

Immediate prerequisites:

- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/quadratic-presentation
- PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/fitting-extension
- tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-1-nodes-normalization-and-dual-graphs

Acceptance controls:

- C = 0: A = B, A′ = B′ and both sides are Fitt(B)Fitt(B′).
- B = B′, A = A′: trivial identity.
- R = Z, C = Z/2, B = Z/4 and B′ = Z/6 with their reductions to Z/2: A = 2Z/4Z ≅ Z/2, A′ = 2Z/6Z ≅ Z/3, and Fitt(A)·Fitt(B′) = (2)(6) = (12) = (3)(4) = Fitt(A′)·Fitt(B); the fibre product is cyclic of order 12. The other pairing fails: Fitt(A)·Fitt(B) = (8) ≠ (18) = Fitt(A′)·Fitt(B′).

- DK-arXiv-v3 — Lemma 2.7 and proof, arXiv v3 PDF p. 18. Lemma 2.7 with its fibre-product proof; ‘A and A′ finitely presented’ is made explicit.

#### The order of the cokernel of a square matrix over a principal ideal domain

**PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6/pid-cokernel-cardinality** — lemma.

Let D be a principal ideal domain (possibly a field) and A an m×m matrix over D with det A ≠ 0. Then D^m/AD^m is finite if and only if D/(det A) is finite, and in that case #(D^m/AD^m) = #(D/(det A)).

Proposed declaration: `TauCeti.natCard_quotient_range_toLin'_of_det_ne_zero`.

Hypotheses and carriers:

- D is a commutative principal ideal domain; fields, finite or infinite, are allowed. Only det A ≠ 0 is assumed.
- With the convention that the cardinality of an infinite quotient is 0 (Nat.card), the statement is the single equality #(D^m/AD^m) = #(D/(det A)).

Construction or proof route:

- If D is finite, it is a field (Finite.isField_of_domain) and det A is a unit; then A·adj(A) = det(A)·I (Matrix.mul_adjugate) shows that A is surjective, and both quotients are 0.
- Let D be infinite. A is injective on D^m: Av = 0 gives det(A)·v = adj(A)·A·v = 0 (Matrix.adjugate_mul), so v = 0. Hence A is an isomorphism of D^m onto N = AD^m, so N is a submodule of full rank m (finrank N = finrank D^m), and Submodule.quotientEquivPiSpan, applied to N and the standard basis of D^m, gives D^m/AD^m ≅ ∏_{i=1}^m D/(x_i), where x_i is the i-th coefficient Submodule.smithNormalFormCoeffs of N. These coefficients come with a basis b′ of D^m (Submodule.smithNormalFormTopBasis) and a basis of N with the same index set (Submodule.smithNormalFormBotBasis) whose i-th vector is x_i·b′_i (Submodule.smithNormalFormBotBasis_def).
- det A is associated to ∏ x_i: the inclusion N ⊆ D^m composed with the isomorphism D^m ≅ N given by A is A, of determinant det A; composed with the isomorphism D^m ≅ N that sends b′_i to the i-th vector x_i·b′_i of the basis of N, it is the endomorphism of D^m that is diagonal with entries x_i in the basis b′, of determinant ∏ x_i. Two composites of the inclusion with isomorphisms D^m ≅ N have associated determinants (LinearMap.associated_det_comp_equiv).
- For nonzero a, b in the infinite principal ideal domain D, a Dedekind domain: #(D/(ab)) = #(D/(a))·#(D/(b)), with the value 0 for an infinite quotient (cardQuot_mul). Hence #(D/(det A)) = #(D/(∏ x_i)) = ∏_i #(D/(x_i)) = #(D^m/AD^m), and one side is finite exactly when the other is.

Immediate prerequisites:

- mathlib:Matrix.mul_adjugate
- mathlib:Matrix.adjugate_mul
- mathlib:Finite.isField_of_domain
- mathlib:Submodule.quotientEquivPiSpan
- mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalFormCoeffs
- mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalFormTopBasis
- mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalFormBotBasis
- mathlib:Submodule.smithNormalFormBotBasis_def
- mathlib:LinearMap.associated_det_comp_equiv
- mathlib:cardQuot_mul
- mathlib:Submodule.natAbs_det_equiv

Acceptance controls:

- D = Z, A = [[2, 1], [0, 3]]: det A = 6 and Z²/AZ² is cyclic of order 6.
- D = F_ℓ[t], A = diag(t, t): #(D²/AD²) = ℓ² = #(D/(t²)).
- D a field: det A ≠ 0 means that A is invertible, and both quotients are trivial.
- m = 1: the statement is the identity #(D/aD) = #(D/(a)).
- D = Z: the statement is #(Z^m/AZ^m) = |det A|, which is Mathlib's Submodule.natAbs_det_equiv applied to the isomorphism Z^m ≅ AZ^m given by A; the proof here is the same argument with cardQuot_mul in place of Int.natAbs.
